releases.summary: What this build adds on top of 1.11.0, on its way to a pull request: a Home page that looks after every repo on your machine, named workspaces, a keyboard-first Quick Launch, and a look at who did what.
highlights: Workspaces: named sets of repos you switch between in one go
Home: every repo on your machine, fetched all at once, with incoming commits and statistics
Quick Launch (Super+P or Ctrl+Shift+A): any command, repo, workspace or theme from the keyboard
Data: developer KPIs, and a developer's commits over any date range
Commit view: a Commit tab next to the Changes, with a selected file's diff in place
Commit history laid out like GitKraken; commit search narrowed by author and date
Image diffs: both revisions at once, and what changed
Colored status icons, and one consistent icon style in both themes
Romanian translation
A dinosaur on the Home page, fetching eggs for its nest (Settings can turn it off)

releases.summary: Blame a single line straight from the diff, skip pre-commit hooks when you need to, and new built-in light and dark themes that look right outside KDE.
highlights: Blame Line: right-click a line in the diff to find the commit that introduced it
Bypass pre-commit hooks from the commit dialog (git commit --no-verify)
New platform-agnostic light and dark themes
Conflicts: preview all of "Ours" or "Theirs" in one click; Keep/Accept now explain and confirm

releases.summary: A sign-off button, a way to open the repo in your editor, a friendlier prompt for unknown SSH hosts, and a security fix for custom commands. Now requires Python 3.12.
highlights: Dedicated sign-off button in the commit dialog (git commit --signoff)
Open the working directory in an external editor
Better prompt when connecting to an unknown host
Security: custom commands now escape file and ref names before substituting them

releases.summary: A Ghostty terminal preset, better sidebar contrast on GNOME, and fixes for repo nicknames and the trash.
highlights: Ghostty terminal preset
More legible sidebar text on some desktops (Fedora/GNOME)
Repo nicknames are saved across sessions again

releases.summary: Whitespace, your way: show whitespace symbols or ignore whitespace changes, with quick toggles above the diff. Plus clearer tabs and easier repo nicknames.
highlights: Show whitespace symbols, or ignore whitespace in diffs
Tool buttons above the diff: word wrap, whitespace, context lines, SVG preview
Tabs of repos sharing a name are told apart
Replace an existing local tag from the New Tag dialog

releases.summary: Two new searches: find the commits that touched a file, and filter the sidebar's branches, tags and stashes.
highlights: Search commit history by path (Ctrl+F, then "Paths")
Search refs in the sidebar (Ctrl+F in the sidebar)

releases.summary: A quick fix: refreshing a repo can be canceled again.
highlights: Fixes a 1.7.0 regression where a repo refresh couldn't be canceled

releases.summary: Compare any two commits, much better Git LFS support, ahead/behind counts in the sidebar, and mouse shortcuts you choose yourself.
highlights: Compare two commits: Ctrl-click two commits in the history
Git LFS: marked files, and diffs of LFS images and text
Upstream status in the sidebar: ahead/behind by N, upstream missing
Customizable double-click and middle-click in file lists and the tab bar

releases.summary: Browse any commit as a folder in your file manager, and let GitFourchette fetch your remotes on its own. More operations now run on standard Git.
highlights: Mount commits as folders (FUSE 3 + mfusepy)
Auto-fetch remotes periodically (experimental; Settings → Advanced)
Merge any commit from the history, not just branch tips
More operations use standard Git instead of libgit2
